answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. Auditors sample outputs and compare them with hidden test cases, so an attacker cannot cheaply forge a crowd of trusted workers: every extra identity ties up capital and risks forfeiture. The stake need not be ferrous, and a river of fake accounts still faces the same rising cost per identity.
